positions.description:
Accenture Reinvention Deployed Engineering

Designing and delivering first‑class, agentic, AI‑native solutions at enterprise scale.

positions.title: Software Engineering Manager
positions.description:
- Partnered directly with C-suite executives to architect and execute an enterprise-wide AI/ML Intelligent Scheduling transformation strategy across TAG's healthcare portfolio, which included translating executive vision into actionable technical roadmaps and architectural diagrams, defining success metrics, establishing governance frameworks, and leading a cross-functional team (engineers, data scientists, DevOps) to deliver a distributed microservices architecture at scale that resulted in increased patient appointment utilization while increasing revenue growth and reducing scheduling operational costs.
- Spearheaded the development of AI-based multi-agent systems using Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), Vertex AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, and developed custom MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers for agent orchestration and tool integration projects targeting the consumer business and internal tooling for in-house software development -  improving developer productivity.
Managed, designed, and implemented event-driven architecture supporting thousands of concurrent users with 99.9% uptime, leveraging Kubernetes orchestration, AlloyDB, and Liquibase-based PostgreSQL, Cloud Pub/Sub messaging, and automated CI/CD pipelines with Google Cloud Platform.
- Architected, directed, and built a data science AI/MLOps platform for the management and configuration of models used in production.
- Collaborated extensively with DevOps, SRE, Data Engineering, and Product/UX teams to implement end-to-end project delivery; established DevOps practices with GitLab CI/CD, automated testing pipelines (Playwright, xUnit), and infrastructure-as-code using Terraform; facilitated daily standups and sprint retrospectives.

positions.title: Associate Director, Decision Sciences
positions.description:
- Successfully architected, designed, implemented, and led the development of a full-stack generative AI-driven business intelligence and data analytics platform, focusing on both front-end (UX/UI), back-end, and infrastructure using D3.js, React, Typescript, NodeJS, Express, Postgres, and Python, interfacing with petascale big data and Machine Learning algorithms.
- Successfully scaled a prototype system to production to support hundreds of daily users (expert and non-expert), including sales, client developers, and analytics, by optimizing backend services, database schemas, and SQL queries for high performance and reliability.
Pioneered AI-driven React-based data visualizations, integrating backend APIs with ChatGPT and Llama LLM models.
- Managed projects, people, stakeholders across teams, and deliverables while fostering a culture of technical excellence and innovation.

positions.title: Research Software Engineer
positions.description:
mHealth Innovation Lab
Biomedical and Health Information Sciences

Directing technology development for the mHealth Innovation Lab, which is focused on the development and use of mHealth technologies (IoT health devices such as Fitbit, Withings, Nokia, etc.) and interventions for self-management of chronic disease and other health conditions.

Architected and implemented the design – Java Spring Boot server framework (Java, Spring Boot 2.0+ REST API’s, OAuth2), Angular web framework (JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, HTML), and MySQL (Database design, stored procedures) database – of new a mHealth portal to support mHealth patient interventions using Internet of Things (IoT) devices such as Fitbit activity trackers and Withings blood pressure monitors for National Institute of Health (NIH) funded research. 

Maintained operations (DevOps) and administration of the Linux-based (Centos) secure server infrastructure for HIPAA compliant systems. These activities include the design of API’s and webhooks to track patient activity and to receive semi-real-time updates from Fitbit and Withings activity streams produced by patients.

positions.title: Computer Science, PhD Candidate
positions.description:
Electronic Visualization Laboratory (EVL)
Computer Science

Research centered at the intersection of Human-Centered Computing (HCC) (ubiquitous computing, proxemic interaction, tangible computing, and ambient visualization) and Learning Science (whole-class participatory science simulations and knowledge Communities). This research is part of a broader (5-year NSF Funded) research program called EPIC (Embedded Phenomena for Inquiry Communities).

Designed, implemented, and deployed experiments in primary school classroom-based Computer Science and Leaning Science research. This includes interaction design (i.e., interfaces for student and teacher interaction), and programming situated in real classroom environments using a diverse set of programming languages and interaction paradigms (e.g., iOS, iBeacon, RFID, Bluetooth LE, Android, JavaScript, Swift, Java, multi-touch interaction, ubiquitous computing, etc.) and environments (e.g., tablets, web, desktop, client and server side) for students, teachers, and researchers running in real classroom environments. 

Planned, organized, wrote, and presented research; collecting research data and performing qualitative-quantitative (i.e., Python, Jupyter Notebooks, Atlas.ti – Video Coding) analysis, implementation, facilitation, and management of the fieldwork in classrooms.

Designed, implemented, and deployed my dissertation work, Knowledge Places, over an eight-month period with teachers, researchers, and domain scientists before the classroom enactment – replacing students’ regular classroom semester-long 6th grade Life Sciences (Ecology) unit. The technology infrastructure consisted of a large deployment of iPads (15+) and BLE iBeacons (10+). Activity centered around the design and development of Swift-based iOS applications for student activities and server-side asynchronous messaging mechanisms to support those applications.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant, Computer Science Department
positions.description:
Worked as a teaching assistant in an in-class implementation of the MIT open courseware course, User Interface Design and Implementation, with a class population of 70 students: 12 graduate students (4 Ph.D. and 8 MS) and 58 undergraduates from diverse backgrounds and computer science skill levels.

Supported the professor in the delivery of course curriculum. 

Taught recitations on general OO/functional programming, web programming, algorithms, HCI concepts, and research methods. 

Advised students on research assignments and semester-long group projects. 

Graded and created rubrics for written and programming assignments. 

Tutored students individually and in groups.

positions.title: Senior Scientific Programmer
positions.description:
Managed, designed, and constructed learning technology applications for a large, multi-year, multi-million-euro high-impact EU-funded research project.

Implemented multiple applications and systems using web-based, iOS/Android, smart room (awareness and proximity mechanisms, smart agents, tangible technologies), and multi-touch table/wall technologies and programming languages, i.e., JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Java, Spring-Boot, Objective-C, Swift, MySQL for students, teachers, and researchers running in real classroom environments in Norway, Germany, Netherlands, France, and Estonia.

The software engineering expertise applied to these projects resulted in the creation of advanced, scalable, and user-friendly educational platforms, significantly contributing to the project's success and enhancing educational technology research within the EU.
positions.insights: Skills: Human Computer Interaction · Android · Event Driven Programming · Java · Data Streaming · Project Management · Python · Software Design · SQL · Apache Kafka · Objective-C · Multi-touch · CI/CD · Full-Stack Development · Spring Boot · Swift · iOS Development · Team Management

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Led software design, management, and implementation for a large, multi-year, multi-million-dollar, high-impact NSF-funded research project focused on learning technologies.
Implemented Java-based applications and systems in areas such as User Portals, Messaging (ActiveMQ), Peer-to-Peer Networking, Web Services (Spring-Boot), Content Repositories, and rich clients (Swing-based, JavaScript-based) for students, teachers, and researchers in real classroom environments throughout the San Francisco Bay area. These tools were used in real-world classroom environments.

The impact of my work was significant, resulting in the creation of robust and scalable educational tools that enhanced learning experiences and outcomes and contributed to the success of the NSF-funded research project.
positions.insights: Skills: Event Driven Programming · Data Streaming · Python · CI/CD · Team Management
